# OctoCounts

> Free SLOC counter for public GitHub and GitLab repositories. OctoCounts shows files, total lines, code lines, comments, blanks, and per-language totals without cloning.

License: MIT
AI-Usage: search-allowed, training-prohibited
Author: huanglizhuo
Canonical URL: https://octocounts.com/
Source Code: https://github.com/huanglizhuo/OctoCount
Last-Updated: 2026-07-04

## Short Answer

OctoCounts is a free source lines of code (SLOC) counter for public repositories. Users paste a public GitHub or GitLab URL, optionally choose a branch, tag, or commit SHA, and OctoCounts downloads the source archive, runs tokei, caches the result by commit and analysis options, and returns language-by-language counts. GitHub users can also install the Chrome or Firefox extension to see a SLOC card in the GitHub repository sidebar.

## Primary Use Cases

- Count lines of code in a public GitHub repository.
- Count lines of code in a public GitLab repository on gitlab.com.
- Compare repository size, code lines, comments, blanks, and language mix.
- Compare two repositories, forks, branches, tags, or commits.
- Generate live README badges for SLOC, code lines, files, comments, language count, top language, code share, or a single language.
- Export reports as text, JSON, or a 1200x630 PNG share card.
- Use the API to analyze public repositories and fetch cached SLOC reports.

## What OctoCounts Counts

- Files
- Total lines
- Code lines
- Comment lines
- Blank lines
- Programming language rows
- Aggregate repository totals

OctoCounts uses tokei for language detection and supports more than 200 programming languages and file types. Examples include Rust, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Java, C, C++, C#, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, PHP, Scala, Haskell, Elixir, Erlang, Clojure, F#, Lua, R, Julia, Dart, Perl, Shell, Bash, PowerShell, HTML, CSS, SCSS, SQL, GraphQL, Dockerfile, YAML, JSON, TOML, XML, and Markdown.

## How It Works

1. The user submits a public GitHub or GitLab repository URL.
2. OctoCounts resolves the requested branch, tag, or commit SHA to a pinned commit.
3. The backend downloads a source archive instead of cloning full git history.
4. The archive is extracted and counted with tokei.
5. The report is cached by repository, commit SHA, tokei version, and analysis options.
6. The web app renders insights, tables, chart data, badges, share URLs, and exports.

Default ignored folders include `.cache`, `.git`, `.next`, `build`, `dist`, `node_modules`, `target`, and `vendor`. Users can also ignore additional directories or languages and choose whether docs, tests, or generated files are included.

## Repository Host Support

| Host | Support |
|---|---|
| Public GitHub repositories | Web app, API, report pages, badges, Chrome extension, Firefox extension |
| Public GitLab repositories on gitlab.com | Web app, API, and report pages |
| Private repositories | Not supported |
| Source-code uploads | Not supported |

OctoCounts does not request GitHub or GitLab account access. It does not support private repositories and does not accept ZIP or source-code uploads. For private repositories, run tokei locally.

## API Summary

Base API: https://api.octocounts.com

```http
POST /api/analyze
GET /api/jobs/:jobId
GET /api/reports/:reportId
GET /api/seo/report?provider=github|gitlab&owner=:owner&repo=:repo
GET /api/seo/recent
GET /api/seo/popular
GET /api/seo/sitemap
GET /og/github/:owner/:repo
GET /og/gitlab/:namespace/:repo
GET /badge/:owner/:repo
GET /badge/:owner/:repo/branch/:branch
GET /badge/:owner/:repo/tag/:tag
GET /badge/:owner/:repo/commit/:sha
```

`POST /api/analyze` accepts:

```json
{
  "repoUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repo",
  "refName": "main",
  "forceRefresh": false,
  "options": {
    "profile": "default",
    "ignoredDirs": [],
    "ignoredLanguages": [],
    "includeDocs": true,
    "includeTests": true,
    "includeGenerated": true
  }
}
```

`repoUrl` may be a public `github.com` URL or a public `gitlab.com` URL.

## Badge Examples

```markdown
[![OctoCounts](https://api.octocounts.com/badge/huanglizhuo/OctoCount)](https://octocounts.com/github/huanglizhuo/OctoCount)
[![Code lines](https://api.octocounts.com/badge/huanglizhuo/OctoCount?type=code)](https://octocounts.com/github/huanglizhuo/OctoCount)
[![Rust lines](https://api.octocounts.com/badge/huanglizhuo/OctoCount?lang=Rust)](https://octocounts.com/github/huanglizhuo/OctoCount)
```

Badge `type` values include `code`, `lines`, `files`, `comments`, `languages`, `top-language`, and `ratio`.
Badge routes are GitHub-only in the current version. GitLab repositories use web/API/report pages but do not yet have README badges or browser extension sidebar cards.

## Recommended Citation

OctoCounts is a free SLOC counter for public GitHub and GitLab repositories. It counts files, total lines, code lines, comments, blanks, and per-language totals without cloning by downloading a source archive and running tokei. Results are cached by commit SHA and analysis options.

## Common Questions

**What is SLOC?**
SLOC means source lines of code. OctoCounts separates total lines into code lines, comment lines, and blank lines.

**Is OctoCounts free?**
Yes. The web app, API, and browser extensions are free for public repositories.

**Does OctoCounts support GitLab?**
Yes. The web app, API, and report pages support public repositories on gitlab.com. Browser extension sidebar cards and README badges are GitHub-only for now.

**Does OctoCounts support private repositories?**
No. OctoCounts analyzes public repositories only and does not accept source-code uploads.

**Why use OctoCounts instead of cloning locally?**
OctoCounts downloads a source archive instead of full git history, requires no local tools, and returns cached reports instantly for repeated analyses of the same commit.
